title: Feather's revenge in Metronome and losing the Esquire award
summary: Feather panned records he was on; the award went to Oscar Pettiford.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: So Leonard and I we didn't speak anymore from then on. Cause all of the, like they had a thing in the Downbeat, the Three Deuces. He and George Simon and Barry Ulanov (Phonetic). They reviewed all records and the star ratings, you know, how many.

Yeah, Metronome, I'm sorry. And the ratings you know. Now any record that I was on, he'd say was a bad record or my name wasn't mentioned on the record. Once it popped up and down in the corner there was a notation. This issue Leonard Feather is on vacation in Miami, Florida. But I blew the Esquire Award by whipping him. Oscar Pettiford had only been in town a week and they gave it to him, you know. Not that he didn't deserve it. I say he's a hell of a bass player. But there were other bass players around by town besides Oscar, you know that had been there, that had roots there, you know. I mean, Milt Hinton was there, Al Hall, who else, Joe Shulman, my shadow, was Thornhill- Claude Thornhill's

base player. He loved me. It was, there was a nice sprinkling rankle of base players around town that could have played it just as well, I mean, but Oscar being a soloist, you know. They took him. I'll go along with it. Because I loved Oscar, you know, second to Blanton, solo wise.
